Jason —

Thanks again for agreeing to run the hands-on POC with us. We'd like to lock a 90-minute kickoff + working session where we'll: 
- walk through the proposed POC agenda (attached poc-agenda.pdf),
- review prompts and routing rules you want to validate,
- run a short tethered load/benchmark (test-harness review + load-test-config.yaml attached), and
- set throughput targets and latency SLOs for the formal benchmark run.

Proposed windows (PT):
- Tues Apr 18, 10:00–11:30
- Wed Apr 19, 14:00–15:30
- Thu Apr 20, 09:00–10:30

Please confirm which window works for your team and whether Procurement should be on for the kickoff. Our internal asks for the session: a small sample of production prompts, a list of routing/priority rules you care about, and a contact who can approve short-term burst capacity if we need to scale during the run.

Attachments: poc-agenda.pdf, load-test-config.yaml

Cheers,
Olga Petrov
Senior Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference

+1 415 555 0198

Jason / Olga —

Great — Wed Apr 19 14:00 PT is in my calendar. Quick notes on the measurement plan so Procurement and SREs have expectations: 
- Throughput target: we'll validate up to ~3,500 tokens/sec aggregate (this aligns with your 3k target and gives a buffer). We'll also validate 150–250 concurrent sessions (we'll parameterize in the config).
- Latency SLOs: target p95 <= 350 ms for 1–2k token prompts, p99 <= 700 ms; tail behavior will be noted for larger prompts.
- Metrics we will collect: p50/p95/p99 latency, tokens/sec, requests/sec, GPU utilization, memory, and model KV cache hit rates. We'll provide sample dashboards and a short runbook in the repo.

Technical attachments: load-test-config.yaml (attached) includes the scenario seeds, concurrency profile, and workload replay mapping. The test harness (https://git.redwood.dev/poc/load-test-harness) is k6-based with a replay client that can drive tokens-based load. We recommend running a 10-minute warmup then 20-minute runs per profile.

Procurement: we can provide sanitized logs for the demo. If you need full audit logs we can share the retention policy doc during the session — tagging @olga to confirm distribution.

If ACME has any specific routing priorities (VIP users, routing by prompt type), please send them before Tue so Grace can update the routing rules and we can test canary fallbacks.

Thanks,
Rishi Malhotra
Staff Infra Engineer | Redwood Inference
rishi_malhotra@redwood.com

From: Dev Patel <dev_patel@redwood.com>

Jason —

Small technical notes for the working session and what we'll demo live: 
- Routing: we'll show priority routing (VIP -> low-latency tier) and automatic fallback to a smaller quantized model if the primary model reaches configured CPU/GPU thresholds. We'll include a canary rollout so you can see gradual traffic shifts.
- Batching: for throughput tests we'll toggle batching on vs off; batching increases throughput but can affect tail latency. We'll annotate runs in the dashboard so you can compare.
- KV cache priming: bring a 50–100 prompt prefix sample so we can demonstrate prefix caching impact on latency.
- Test harness: the harness supports replaying recorded prompt traces and can inject synthetic jitter to emulate real clients. See redwood-test-harness-instructions.md in attachments for quick start.

I'll prepare two sample configs for the session: a conservative profile (150 concurrent, 2k tokens/sec) and an aggressive profile (250 concurrent, 4k tokens/sec). We'll start with conservative and optionally move up if capacity and tail latency look good.

If Procurement wants a short statement on data handling, we can paste that into the calendar invite and attach a sanitized logs example.

Cheers,
Dev Patel
Platform Engineer | Redwood Inference
dev_patel@redwood.com
